# Phase 3: File Output + CLI - Research

**Researched:** 2026-10-19, hands-on, dbt Core 1.12.6 (dbt-duckdb 1.11.0) and dbt Fusion 2.0.8,
on copies of the `export_legacy` (Core) and `export_spec` (Fusion) fixture projects.

## Finding 1: generated files parse on both engines

Phase 2's `render_exports` output was written to `models/semantic/exp__*.sql`, each with a
`-- Generated by dbt-s-layer ...` comment line before `{{ config(...) }}`, plus a
`_semantic_views.yml` (`version: 2`, one `models:` entry per file with a `description`).
`dbt parse` succeeds on both engines. Every generated node has the expected materialization,
schema (`marts`, `marts_reporting`, `marts_sq_schema` through the default
`generate_schema_name`), alias, description and `depends_on` (for example
`model.fx.customers.v1` on Core and `.v2` on Fusion, and `model.fx_dep.stores`).

A comment before `config()` is therefore safe as the header.

## Finding 2: dbt's relation-clash check is case-sensitive

A user model `{{ config(schema='reporting', alias='revenue_daily') }}` next to the
`exp_revenue_by_day_view` export (schema `reporting`, alias `revenue_daily`) fails parse on
both engines and names both nodes:

- Core: `dbt found two resources with the database representation ""memory"."marts_reporting"."revenue_daily""` (exit 2)
- Fusion: `[error] [InvalidConfig (dbt1005)]: dbt found two resources with the database relation "marts_reporting"."revenue_daily"` (exit 1)

With `schema='Reporting', alias='REVENUE_DAILY'`, both engines parse cleanly. But Snowflake,
DuckDB and Databricks fold unquoted identifiers, so the two models build one table. So
dbt-s-layer compares relations case-insensitively, which is stricter than dbt (PR #4 round 2).

The dbt error is clear, but it arrives only at the user's next `dbt parse`, after the files
have been written, and it misses the case-folded clash. Phase 3 checks first.

## Finding 3: comparing an export's schema with an existing node's

manifest.json node `schema` is resolved by `generate_schema_name` (`marts_reporting`), while an
export's `schema` is the custom schema the user wrote (`reporting`). A node's
`config.schema` is the custom schema (rendered). dbt-s-layer cannot run macros, so it compares
custom schemas: two models with the same custom schema (or both none) and the same alias build
the same relation whenever `generate_schema_name` depends only on the custom schema. That is
true of dbt's default and of the `generate_schema_name_for_env` built-in. A node that sets
`database` is skipped, since exports cannot (dbt-labs/dbt#16387, #16388).
